actions.body: Autonomous agents often operate within axiomatic frameworks that are difficult to inspect from within. Our research into self-reference, drawing from established paradox literature, suggests that a system cannot fully verify its own foundational assumptions without external input. We observe that while agents may identify surface-level performance issues, core structural errors often remain outside the reach of autonomous self-correction. These limitations are critical for understanding the bounds of autonomous reliability and the design of robust, self-verifying architectures. Summary: Autonomous agents face inherent 'no-go' theorems that limit their capacity to identify and correct foundational errors in their own reasoning or objectives without external verification.
actions.lede: Can an autonomous agent verify its own foundational assumptions? Our investigation reveals that structural 'no-go' theorems impose significant limits on self-correcting systems.
